claims.text: Al concentration governs phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Increasing or optimizing Al promotes fine, ordered L12 γ′ precipitates within an FCC γ matrix.
A γ + γ′ microstructure retards grain or precipitate coarsening during high-temperature exposure.
The γ + γ′ microstructure retards detrimental phase transformations during environmental and radiation exposure.
The γ + γ′ microstructure enhances deformation twinning and thereby supports cryogenic toughness.
An as-cast or additively manufactured equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy tends to be predominantly FCC.
The predominantly FCC baseline may be unstable under service conditions.
Finely dispersed γ′ precipitates act as barriers to solute diffusion.
Finely dispersed γ′ precipitates suppress unwanted phase separation.
Al addition increases lattice distortion.
Al addition encourages local ordering and facilitates γ′ nucleation and stabilization.
γ′ precipitates impede irradiation-driven diffusion and transformations to deleterious secondary phases.
Optimizing Al will produce a higher volume fraction of fine γ′ precipitates and a γ + γ′ microstructure relative to the baseline.
The optimized γ + γ′ alloy will have improved high-temperature strength relative to the baseline.
The optimized γ + γ′ alloy will have improved oxidation resistance relative to the baseline.
The optimized γ + γ′ alloy will have improved radiation tolerance relative to the baseline.
The optimized γ + γ′ alloy will have superior cryogenic toughness relative to the baseline.
Processing near 800 °C provides a high γ′ fraction with a low coarsening rate.
Al content below the proposed compositional window fails to induce γ′ formation.
Excessive Al in the target alloy leads to precipitation of Ni2AlTi.

contradictions.description: The target and controlled intervention specify the quinary Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system with only Al varied, but the upper-bound failure mode is Ni2AlTi, which requires Ti that is absent from the stated alloy.

The design says that only Al concentration changes while all other elemental concentrations remain constant. For normalized atomic-percent compositions, changing Al necessarily changes the atomic percentages of the other elements unless 'constant' means only that their mutual ratios are fixed.
